question: Rules for making three.js look good and run smoothly on an iPhone inside an Expo React Native app's WebView (react-native-webview, WKWebView): performance budget, iOS WebKit specifics, WebView integration, battery/thermal.

claims.claim: Current three.js WebGLRenderer requires WebGL 2; WebGL 1 was dropped in r163, so the target WebKit must provide WebGL 2.
claims.quote: WebGL 1 is not supported since `r163`.

claims.claim: WebKit has supported WebGL 2 since Safari 15, and its WebGL implementation runs on Metal.
claims.quote: WebKit now supports WebGL2 (demos). In addition, the WebGL implementation now runs on top of Metal for better performance.

claims.claim: Import maps (needed for bare 'three' specifiers without a build step) are listed as a new feature in Safari 16.4 (post dated 2023-03-27; Safari 16.4 runs on iOS 16). NOTE: the quote is the opening part of the sentence only; the fetch tool truncated the remainder ('...without the need for a build step', as paraphrased by the tool).
claims.quote: JavaScript Import Maps give web developers the same sort of versioned file mapping used in other module systems,

claims.claim: Setting the renderer pixel ratio to the full devicePixelRatio is a major cost on phones: a three.js maintainer (Mugen87, 2018-11-16) states that it can kill performance even for simple scenes.
claims.quote: Even with simple scenes this can kill performance.

claims.claim: Measured (user report, 2018-11-16, old hardware): an iOS device was limited to 40 fps with setPixelRatio(window.devicePixelRatio) even on a near-empty scene, and returned to 60 fps when the line was removed.
claims.quote: I got 40 fps on ios mobile devices (not tested on other mobile devices).

claims.claim: Common forum guidance (looeee, three.js collaborator, 2019-04-28) is to clamp pixel ratio to a maximum of 2 or 3.
claims.quote: Usually, you'll set a max pixel ratio of 2 or 3 and clamp to that.

claims.claim: An adaptive alternative to a fixed cap: gkjohnson (three.js collaborator, 2019-04-28) suggests lowering pixel ratio until a target frame rate (example: 55 fps) is reached, because the right value depends on hardware.
claims.quote: So you could decrease the pixel ratio until you hit 55 fps, for example.

claims.claim: A recent (2026-11-06) forum resource describes an adaptive pixel-ratio ladder for phones that starts at 1 and steps 1 -> 1.25 -> 1.5, never exceeding devicePixelRatio, on screens whose native ratio is 2.6 to 3.
claims.quote: It starts at 1 and tries 1 → 1.25 → 1.5, never above devicePixelRatio.

claims.claim: Draw-call budget per the react-three-fiber docs: at most 1000 draw calls, ideally a few hundred or fewer (each mesh is one draw call). NOTE: the quote is the tail fragment of a longer sentence; the fetch tool would not return the full sentence.
claims.quote: no more than 1000 as the very maximum, and optimally a few hundred or less.

claims.claim: A continuous 60-times-per-second render loop is the main battery drain; when the scene comes to rest, rendering should stop (render on demand).
claims.quote: But if the moving parts in your scene are allowed to come to rest, then it would be wasteful to keep rendering.

claims.claim: The r3f docs name the always-on loop as the main battery drain.
claims.quote: This is what generally drains batteries the most and makes fans spin up.

claims.claim: three.js official docs advise driving the loop with renderer.setAnimationLoop rather than a manual requestAnimationFrame (setAnimationLoop(null) is then the stop switch for pausing).
claims.quote: Applications are advised to always define the animation loop with this method and not manually with `requestAnimationFrame()` for best compatibility.

claims.claim: The WebGLRenderer 'antialias' option toggles MSAA on the default framebuffer (it is a constructor option, so it cannot be changed after creation).
claims.quote: Whether to use the default MSAA or not.

claims.claim: On iOS the WKWebView content process is outside the app's RAM accounting and can be terminated independently by the OS to free memory; react-native-webview exposes onContentProcessDidTerminate to detect this (so the app should reload the WebView there). NOTE: quote is the first part of the sentence; the tool reported it continues 'for new apps the user is opening.'
claims.quote: For instance, since iOS WebViews are not included in the total RAM of the app, they can be terminated independently of the app to liberate memory

claims.claim: The WebView -> React Native bridge is only injected when onMessage is set.
claims.quote: You must set onMessage or the window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage method will not be injected into the web page.

claims.claim: Bridge messages must be strings (JSON.stringify any structured payload).
claims.quote: window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage only accepts one argument which must be a string.

claims.claim: When passing inline HTML via source={{ html, baseUrl }}, baseUrl is what relative links in that HTML resolve against (relevant for pointing module/asset URLs at the LAN API server).
claims.quote: The base URL to be used for any relative links in the HTML.

claims.claim: Loading local static HTML with local assets is documented by react-native-webview as not working, with a local web server named as a workaround (supports the serve-over-LAN approach).
claims.quote: Possible workarounds include bundling all assets with webpack or similar, or running a local webserver.

claims.claim: Expo SDK 58 docs (breadcrumb 'Reference (v58.0.0)') list react-native-webview as included in Expo Go for Android and iOS, installed with 'npx expo install react-native-webview'; page shows 'Recommended version: 14.0.1'.
claims.quote: `react-native-webview` provides a `WebView` component that renders web content in a native view.

claims.claim: The native alternative (expo-gl, used by @react-three/fiber/native) has an incomplete WebGL2 implementation and no argument checking, so invalid arguments can crash natively - a risk the WebView path does not carry.
claims.quote: So, passing invalid arguments may cause a native crash.

claims.claim: expo-gl does not work with remote debugging enabled.
claims.quote: This API does not function as intended with remote debugging enabled.

claims.claim: iOS WebGL 'context lost' failures have been WebKit-level regressions rather than three.js bugs (iOS 17.0 regression, WebKit bug 264684, status RESOLVED FIXED; reporter confirmed fixed in 17.1.1). Maintainer Mugen87, 2023-11-11.
claims.quote: This is not a `three.js` specific issue, it affects all WebGL applications.

claims.claim: Forum guidance on avoiding memory-driven context loss on phones: do not recreate geometries/materials in the render loop, reuse them, and avoid unnecessarily large textures (Lawrence3DPK, 2023-10-09). NOTE: quote is a sentence fragment.
claims.quote: not reusing geometries and materials where possible or generating / applying unnecessarily large textures

not_found: three.js official manual pages (rendering-on-demand, responsive/HD-DPI, shadows, optimize-lots-of-objects): every URL tried returned HTTP 404 (threejs.org/manual/en/<page>.html, without .html, raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/dev/manual/en/<page>.html, github.com blob). The manual's own wording on HD-DPI pixel counts, shadow-map draw cost and render-on-demand is therefore unconfirmed; r3f docs and forum posts were used instead.

Measured cost of MSAA (antialias: true) on iPhone GPUs: not found; the three.js docs only define the option.
Measured cost of shadow maps on mobile and recommended shadow map size for iPhone: not found (manual shadows page 404).

Hard numbers for WKWebView WebGL memory limit, max canvas area, or MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE on current iPhones: not found on WebKit blog, WebKit Bugzilla 264684, or react-native-webview docs. A three.js forum thread titled 'Memory limit crash on iOS 26' appeared in search but was not opened.

contradictions.claim: Whether the iOS 17 WebGL 'context lost' regression was fixed by the 17.1.1 update.

a.quote: Confirm this is no longer an issue with iPadOS 17.1.1 or 17.1.1 I'll close this ticket.

b.quote: We are still experiencing this issue on iOS 17.1.2 phones

contradictions.claim: Whether a fixed maximum pixel ratio is a sound rule on mobile.

a.quote: Usually, you'll set a max pixel ratio of 2 or 3 and clamp to that.

b.quote: It really just depends on the hardware.

contradictions.claim: Whether iOS WebGL crashes over time are avoidable by application-side memory hygiene.

a.quote: It turned out that this is a problem with the browser itself on iOS and there is no way to get rid of it.

b.quote: unless you have some sort of major memory leak such as recreating geometries and / or materials in a render loop,
